Stochastic gradient descent gets the same fast rate from a light adaptive step-size rule that skips line search and special tricks, beating older polynomial-rate guarantees. In both cases, a well-shaped growth in step size alone is enough.
arxiv-2602-19046:
Explicit formulas can make wave simulations exact in time. Yvonne Alama Bronsard, with one co-author, extends that idea in 2026 to the Benjamin-Ono and continuum Calogero-Moser equations on the torus. Discretising the formulas yields schemes exact in time. Only space needs discretisation. Cost stays independent of the final time.

The authors generalise earlier fully-discrete schemes. New versions preserve structure better, including mass and momentum for Benjamin-Ono. Convergence now covers rough solutions, merely square-integrable in the Benjamin-Ono case. That regularity is scaling-critical for Calogero-Moser. The main theorem sends the error norm to zero as truncation grows, uniformly over bounded time intervals. A square-wave test gives the first rigorous numerical evidence of the Talbot effect for Benjamin-Ono.
arxiv-2602-19446:
English has long dominated open-source software, but global participation and Unicode support for non-Latin scripts are changing that. Masudul Hasan Masud Bhuiyan and two co-authors study how multilingual open source is becoming. They analyze GitHub activity from 2015 to 2025 across five programming languages and thirty natural languages. The data set includes 62,500 repositories and billions of GitHub items (9.14 billion issues, pull requests, and discussions).

Multilingual participation has risen steadily, especially in Korean, Chinese, and Russian, appearing in issues, discussions, code comments, string literals, and documentation. The shift brings greater inclusivity and language diversity, but also language tension, as the ability to express oneself in a first language meets community norms. Six research questions track changes across communication, code, and documentation.
arxiv-2602-19546:
Timing pulsars circling a giant black hole can map the spacetime around it with care, testing gravity theory in a new way. Zexin Hu and two co-authors present a true-to-life pulsar-giant black hole timing model built on post-Newtonian motion laws. Future high-rate surveys by new radio dishes like the SKA may find pulsars circling Sagittarius A*, the black hole at our galaxy's heart.

The model adds several next-to-leading-order delays in light travel time, matching hoped-for future timing care. For the first time, it adds the effects of Sgr A*'s proper motion, hoped to break the spin-measure tangle. The paper predicts timing care for varied Sgr A* traits and talks through the data work plan.
arxiv-2602-20046:
CLIP maps images and text into a shared latent space by pulling similar items together and pushing dissimilar ones apart, but its contrast-based losses can leave that space sparse and broken. A 2026 arXiv paper by Eleonora Grassucci and two co-authors studies that modality gap in the medical domain, where it was previously unknown and unresolved.

The gap was partly eased for standard text-image pairs, but medical alignment, with scan images and clinical text, is more complex. The authors confirm the gap is present in medical matching too, and propose a mode-agnostic framework that closes it, so representations related in meaning align better regardless of source mode. Their method improves cross-modal retrieval and image captioning between radiology images and clinical text. Readers gain a framework for tighter medical multimodal matching.
arxiv-2602-20146:
Surface groups act on geometric spaces in rich ways. Bending those actions while tracking entropy reveals where rigid behaviour survives. A 2026 arXiv paper by Martin Bridgeman and two co-authors studies neighbourhoods of the Fuchsian locus inside quasifuchsian space for a closed surface.

The authors show an explicit neighbourhood of the Fuchsian locus exists. Every non-Fuchsian representation inside it admits a proper affine action on the Lie algebra of two-by-two complex matrices with determinant one. Its linear part is given by the adjoint representation. They further show a larger neighbourhood exists. In it, every critical point of the entropy function lies on the Fuchsian locus itself. Readers gain precise statements about how far Fuchsian rigidity extends into quasifuchsian space, for both affine actions and entropy critical points.
arxiv-2602-20246:
Some transitions in the early universe could have left two traces: ripples in spacetime and tiny black holes. Such first-order transitions always happen in theories where symmetries break through radiative effects and masses appear as a result. A 2026 arXiv paper by Alberto Salvio, working alone, reviews a model-independent way to study those transitions when cooling runs far below the symmetry-breaking scale before the transition fires.

In that supercooled regime, standard perturbative tools can still pin down the effective action. The reviewed method turns that into ready-to-use formulas that work for any model of this kind, with no need to redo the analysis case by case. Readers gain a portable toolkit: take a supercooled model, apply the formulas, and read off transition properties relevant to gravitational waves and black hole formation.
arxiv-2602-20346:
Camryn Mullin and fourteen co-authors report time-variable scattered light in disks around Herbig stars, seen with Subaru SCExAO. Nine Herbig stars from a volume-limited sample within two hundred parsecs were imaged in near-infrared polarized light. Disks around MWC 480, HD 163296, and HD 143006 were seen first with SCExAO, and the results were compared with earlier VLT/SPHERE data to hunt for brightness changes.

In MWC 480, two azimuthal brightness dips appear near the disk minor axis, and one appears shifted between 2021 and 2022. In HD 163296, a brightness peak moves along the outer ring over fifteen months, faster than local Keplerian motion would allow. That speed points to changing illumination rather than moving material, though the origin stays uncertain. HD 143006 shows no significant change over ten months, six further targets show no disk, and a first fast-PDI detection demonstrates both promise and limits of that mode.
arxiv-2602-20446:
Capture-the-flag competitions now test AI security skills, but most evaluations test AI alone rather than humans working with AI. Tingxuan Tang and eight co-authors run the first study of AI assistance in a live capture-the-flag event, with forty-one participants. They track perception, trust, and expectations before and after hands-on AI use. They also watch participants collaborate with an AI agent, and four autonomous agents on the same challenges.

As the event progresses, teams hand larger subtasks to the AI, granting it more agency. Solving rates are often limited not by model reasoning but by the players, as weak prompting and poor context-setting become the main bottleneck. Autonomous agents that steer their own prompting and tool use bypass that bottleneck and beat most human teams, finishing second. The authors close with lessons for future challenges and human-in-the-loop security systems.
arxiv-2602-20646:
Stochastic gradient descent for composite optimization has a failure mode when forward and backward passes are perturbed. Boao Kong and two co-authors study tuning with a sequence of operators subject to nudges in both passes. Unlike analyses treating gradient noise as additive and local, the paper shows that nudges to intermediate outputs and gradients cascade through the computational graph, compounding with the operator count.

The paper gives the first full theoretical analysis of this setting. It characterizes how forward and backward nudges propagate and amplify within one gradient step. It derives convergence bounds for non-convex goals and for Polyak-Lojasiewicz goals, and pins down when nudges leave the asymptotic order intact. The analysis explains gradient spiking in deep learning, characterizing when training recovers from spikes or diverges. Tests on logistic regression with convex and non-convex regularization confirm the theory, including lopsided sensitivity to forward versus backward nudges.
arxiv-2602-21346:
Safety lining up in language models often stays shallow: models reject harmful prompts with no grasp of why, leaving them open to jailbreaks that disguise intent. Mengxuan Hu and six co-authors deepen lining up through thought in this 2026 arXiv paper. Causal poking shows the weak spot stems from shallow tools lacking deep thought.

The authors build a chain-of-thought fine-tuning set mixing utility and safety-key prompts with step-by-step reasons, nudging ruled noes grounded in thought. Lining-Up-Weighted Direct Taste Tuning then targets the most tricky output parts, weighting thought and final-answer segments not alike for finer-grained updates than vanilla taste tuning. Trials show steadily better jailbreak toughness while keeping overall utility.
arxiv-2602-21446:
Ziyi Liang and seven co-authors introduce ConformalHDC, a framework that adds firm uncertainty estimates to hyperdimensional computing. That computing style is efficient for brain-like learning. But it lacks firm uncertainty estimates, leaving open decision edges open to outliers, hostile inputs, and strange new data.

ConformalHDC joins conformal prediction promises with HDC speed in two forms. A set-valued form gives finite-sample promises that hold widely, with enclosed edges that resist odd inputs. A point-valued form uses the same fit scores for single predictions, sometimes beating older HDC methods by modeling class links. Applied to decoding test signals from brain spikes during a memory task, it decodes well, reports honest doubt, and rightly abstains on data from other tasks.
arxiv-2602-21546:
Zhi Cao and four co-authors use Mamba sequence modeling to solve flexible job shop planning. The Flexible Job Shop Problem assigns jobs to machines to optimize goals such as minimizing total completion time, with extensive factory and production uses. Current learning-based methods often rely on local feature reading, limiting their grasp of links spanning operations and machines.

The proposed design harnesses Mamba, a state-space model with linear compute cost, for full sequence modeling tailored to the problem. Unlike common graph methods that prove computationally intensive here, the new model is faster. An encoder with a dual Mamba block reads operation and machine features apart. A fast cross-attention decoder then learns linked codes of operations and machines. Tests show faster solving speed and scores surpassing leading learning-based methods across benchmarks.
arxiv-2602-21946:
Yohann Sanvert and nine co-authors report the lab generation of a collective polarization effect in light pulses trapped in a Fabry-Perot Kerr resonator. The device is a passive fiber cavity driven by coherent light, where short pulses called cavity solitons can circulate. Readings of the light's polarization catch pulses tipping from even states into uneven ones.

The tip is set off by a split in polarization driven by cross-phase effects between light parts. More striking, once enough pulses share the cavity, they all settle into the same uneven polarization state, an effect the authors call collective polarization conformity. Because light runs both ways in such cavities, the behavior has no counterpart in ring resonators, opening a new corner of soliton dynamics.
arxiv-2602-22146:
Aligning language models with human feedback often becomes a primal-dual optimization problem, but standard methods only guarantee convergence for an averaged policy, not the final one. Yining Li and two co-authors propose a universal primal-dual framework for safe alignment that unifies several existing methods, from safe RLHF to one-shot and multi-shot variants. It covers multi-objective alignment under expected reward constraints.

On top of that framework they build an optimistic primal-dual algorithm, which uses predictive updates for both primal and dual variables to steady the saddle-point dynamics. The paper proves last-iterate convergence for the method, meaning the actual final policy, not just its average, is guaranteed to settle. For alignment engineers, that is a stronger promise than the field usually offers.
arxiv-2602-22546:
Zhiming Wang and two co-authors argue that the hard part of human-AI teamwork is knowing when to ask. Language-model agents do well on general reasoning but stumble in specialist areas where success needs rare knowledge missing from training. Human experts hold that knowledge, yet their advice is often unstructured and unreliable when pasted straight into a plan.

Their framework, AHCE, treats the expert as a reasoning tool called on by a learned policy, through a Human Feedback Module that decides when and how to request help. In Minecraft trials, task success rose 32 percent on normal tasks and nearly 70 percent on highly difficult tasks, with only minimal human input. The point, the authors say, is to learn how to ask, not merely to ask.
arxiv-2602-22846:
Mohammad Yeghaneh Abkenar and five co-authors sharpen stance classification on controversial topics with emotion words. Arguments about contested issues often appeal to feelings, yet prior stance work rarely used fine-grained emotion analysis systematically, and leaned on non-argumentative texts from narrow domains.

The team expands the Bias-Corrected NRC Emotion Lexicon with DistilBERT embeddings, catching emotionally charged terms the lexicon missed, and feeds it into a neural stance classifier. Across five diverse datasets, the expanded lexicon beat the baseline everywhere by up to about six F1 points. It topped the original lexicon on four sets by up to three points, and beat a language-model approach on nearly all corpora. All resources are released for reuse.
arxiv-2602-22946:
András Patkós computes how isospin symmetry breaking shifts the QCD axion mass scale. The ground state's topology shows in how potential energy density depends on the CP-violating angle, computed here in a three-flavour linear meson model.

An isospin-breaking condensate moves the scale of topological fluctuations by five percent, landing close to lattice QCD determinations. Transparent analytical steps make each correction explicit, from a crude starting estimate of topological susceptibility to a quite accurate final result. Beyond the number, the clear physical reading of every step gives the treatment pedagogical value for students of QCD topology.
arxiv-2602-23146:
Jonathan Giezendanner and nine co-authors recover meter-scale surface weather in part. Near-surface weather varies over tens to hundreds of meters yet stays unseen. The team tests whether this variation can be guessed without solving sky shifts. Joining scattered weather stations, fine Earth views, and coarse sky shifts, they infer heat, dewpoint, and wind at thirty-metre detail across the United States.

Against readings held out in space and time, guesses cut error by eleven to twenty-eight percent against the baseline. Inside held-out quarter-degree grid cells, the method regains more spatial spread than baselines, covering nearly half of heat shifts. The method catches shifting gaps between locations and produces clean patterns tied to terrain and land cover. Past weather, our findings show how scattered readings of a shifting system joined with thick readings of lasting landscape structure regain else unseen spatial shifts.
arxiv-2602-23246:
Rithvik Ramesh and 23 co-authors report the first lab demo of a new class of custom nonlinear solids. Recent gains in chip-scale light devices have come mostly from shaping the setting around old bulk solids, not from boosting their built-in nonlinear response. The new design instead exploits the between-band optical jump in uneven shapes to produce strong second-order response.

Using AlGaAs/GaAs coupled quantum wells in the near-infrared as a test case, the team saw strong second-harmonic making from 1550 nm to 775 nm. Measured response values reached 2750 pm/V, over seven times that of bulk GaAs, and matched quantum math based on close-up images of the layers. Growth pauses cleaned the edges and pushed values toward ideal forecasts, while more complex designs predict up to 7 nm/V. Such designs could enable linked photon making at telecom light waves for chip-scale quantum information handling.
arxiv-2602-23546:
Gaurav Kamath and four co-authors show humans and large language models diverge on probabilistic inferences. These are judgments that are likely, but not strictly forced, given a premise. Thinking models excel at logical and math tasks. Yet their conduct on open-ended, fixed-rule-free guessing has been little studied.

Their ProbCOPA dataset holds 210 handmade chance-based guesses in English. Each was rated for odds by 25 to 30 human raters. Human answers prove graded and varied, showing genuine chance-based judgment. Against eight state-of-the-art thinking models, the models always fail to match human-like spreads. Analysis of model thinking chains reveals a common pattern for judging such guesses. The findings stress the need to test thinking beyond fixed-rule settings.
arxiv-2602-23646:
Spencer J. Magnall and four co-authors use true state rules to inform neutron star post-merger gravity-wave tones. Binary neutron star mergers likely produce hot, rapidly spinning neutron stars past their TOV mass. Gravity-wave output from such remnants offers a unique chance to size up the nuclear state rule at out-of-reach depths and heat.

Current sensor design leans on Einstein flow runs, usually with hybrid heat treatments where a cold state rule gains a heat part. The authors instead use true state rules from the Einstein mean-field model with steady heat treatment. Pooling over state rules and parent masses, peak output tone ranges from about two point five to 4 kHz. That width suggests broadband scopes with kHz reach are needed, doubting some tuned post-merger setups. The new KAGRA high-frequency design suits sizing up post-merger remnants better than the KAGRA broadband design.
arxiv-2602-23746:
Daichi Haraguchi probes human-AI gaps in unclear kanji glyph reading, testing shape against context. High text reading scores do not guarantee that vision-language models share human-like choice patterns when settling doubt. The study straight tests humans and vision-language models using smoothly blended kanji glyph shapes made via a beta-VAE.

Choice edges are estimated in a single-glyph reading task using shape alone. Model answers are tested for matching with human judgments under shape in context, placing an unclear glyph near the human choice edge in word-level context. Human and model choice edges differ in the shape-only task, and shape in context can lift human matching in some cases. The results highlight in-kind conduct gaps, giving base insights toward human-model matching testing.
arxiv-2602-23846:
Wei Lian and Alejandro Guerra-Manzanares present MI squared DAS, a multi-layer intrusion detection framework for industrial Internet of Things networks. The 2026 paper notes that varied devices and shifting traffic expose such networks to novel attacks, while older detectors lean on large labeled sets and miss unseen threats.

The framework layers three defenses. Anomaly-based hierarchical traffic pooling separates normal from attack traffic. Open-set recognition tells known attacks from unknown ones. Incremental learning adapts to new attack types with little labeling. Tests on the Edge-IIoTset dataset show strong results at each layer, from normal-attack separation to known-attack classification and adaptation to new classes. The design offers a scalable, adaptive shield for industrial networks facing evolving threats.
arxiv-2602-24146:
Zitian Li and Wang Chi Cheung study best-arm identification under resource constraints, where testing each alternative consumes limited resources at different rates. The 2026 paper formalizes the problem as best-arm identification with resource constraints. It is motivated by applications where evaluating options is not free and resources vary by option.

The authors propose Successive Halving with Resource Rationing, which weaves resource-aware allocation. The method unifies analysis across stochastic and deterministic consumption settings. It introduces a new effective consumption measure to handle the heterogeneity. The work gives a way to find the best alternative when each test spends from a limited budget.
arxiv-2603-01646:
Lizhe Wan and Jiaqi Yang prove that two-dimensional hydroelastic waves can be steered exactly in this 2026 work. Such waves run on a fluid topped by a thin elastic sheet that bends with the flow. Control comes from outside pressure applied on a chosen patch of the surface.

Working in a periodic setting, they show exact controllability for small start and end states. Exact means the system can be driven from one state to the other, not merely close to it. The pressure patch may be any non-empty open set, however small or placed. The drive can also finish in an arbitrarily short time, a strong form of the claim. Results like this anchor control theory for coupled fluid and elastic systems, where free surfaces move with the flow itself.
arxiv-2603-01746:
Alexandru Manole and Laura-Silvia Diosan test whether learning two linked car tasks at once beats learning each alone. Their 2026 work uses car make and model, a natural hierarchy where each model sits under one make. Most deep learning ignores such structure and trains a lone specialist per task.

The pair compare parallel and cascaded multi-task designs across image networks and transformers. They vary dropout rates and loss weights to see when shared learning helps or hurts. Tests run on two known car photo benchmarks with many makes and models. Multi-task learning helps the image network in almost all settings tried. On the larger, messier benchmark, both model types gain a lot, which supports hierarchy-aware training for fine-grained sorting tasks.
arxiv-2603-01846:
Mengchu Cai, Hai-Yang Du, Xiangyu Jiang, and colleagues from the CLQCD Collaboration pin down bottom quark traits with lattice simulations. Their 2026 work computes the bottom quark mass plus masses and decay constants of bottom mesons. Precision here sharpens probes of matter-antimatter asymmetry, a deep open question in physics.

The team uses an anisotropic clover fermion scheme for the heavy quark on many lattice ensembles. Sixteen ensembles span six lattice spacings and a range of light quark masses. A non-perturbative renormalization method is built and checked through its own predictions. That framework handles the physical bottom mass even on coarse lattices, with errors that shrink in the continuum limit. Using a known bottomonium mass as input, they extract the bottom mass with tight uncertainty. They also give the full S-wave meson spectrum and decay constants for all such mesons.
arxiv-2603-02146:
Guanzheng Chen, Michael Qizhe Shieh, and Lidong Bing improve long-document reasoning in this 2026 paper. Reward-based training helps models reason, but it often fails on long inputs. The usual reward grades only the final answer, which gives weak guidance. Models get no credit for finding the right passage inside a long text.

The team proves that answer-only rewards make the finding step nearly impossible to learn. Their fix, LongRLVR, adds a second reward for picking the correct passage. That reward can be checked directly, so learning gets a strong signal. On tough long-text tests, the method beat standard training for every model tried. One mid-size model gained large jumps on two benchmarks.
arxiv-2603-02246:
Marcin Pietroń, Szymon Piórkowski, Kamil Faber, and colleagues compare speech recognition for Polish in this 2026 study. Their focus is medical talks, where clear transcripts matter for care. New systems use deep networks or transformers to turn speech into text end to end. One setup pairs the Whisper model with a language model that fixes its output.

The team tested that pair against a commercial tool and five open models. Tests used two public Polish speech sets plus medical talks, in clean and degraded sound. Errors were counted at word and letter level. Whisper led all open models by far, the results show. The commercial Scribe tool scored best overall on Polish, for both general and medical speech.
arxiv-2603-02346:
Timothy Zaklama, Max Geier, and Liang Fu present one network that predicts electron ground states in this 2026 paper. Electrons repel and correlate strongly, which makes their lowest-energy wave hard to find. Their Large Electron Model outputs a trial wave for any setting of the system. One trained model covers all coupling strengths and particle counts at once.

The design rests on a universal form for many-electron waves, tuned by system settings. Tests use electrons trapped in a two-dimensional bowl potential. The model predicts charge patterns and ground energies with high accuracy. It handles up to fifty particles and settings never seen in training. The authors frame it as a foundation model for material discovery, grounded in the variational principle.
arxiv-2603-02646:
Yixin Zhang, Yunhao Luo, Utkarsh Mishra, and colleagues present a way to plan long robot tasks with video diffusion models. Diffusion models plan short moves well, but long tasks strain computing power and training data. Older fixes stitch short clips by averaging overlaps, which often yields shaky, mismatched plans.

Their 2026 method links overlapping video chunks in a chain and forces the chunk ends to agree on the cleaned-up picture, not the noisy draft. Message passing, run in sync and out of sync, spreads that agreement across the whole plan with no new training. Tests beat earlier baselines and reached start-goal pairs never seen in training. Long plans stay coherent because every seam is checked.
arxiv-2603-03546:
Radu-Andrei Cioacă and five colleagues fuse satellite and inertial navigation in real time, loosely. Autonomous systems need precise positioning, and satellite signals falter exactly where streets get interesting. Factor graph optimization, which blends satellite fixes with motion-sensor data on one graph, is accurate but usually too heavy for live use. Their 2026 paper builds a loosely coupled version and tests whether it can run in real time.

Loose coupling merges finished position solutions rather than raw signals, which keeps the graph light. On a Hong Kong urban dataset known for canyon-like streets, the method ran in real time and stayed available more often than batch processing versions. The gain costs some positioning accuracy. The authors map the three-way trade-off between accuracy, availability, and computing effort in detail, giving designers honest numbers for live systems.
arxiv-2603-03646:
Mohamed Elmoghany and twenty-nine colleagues, from Adobe Research and partner institutions, generate story videos that can run for an hour without losing the plot. Long-form synthesis usually breaks three ways: backgrounds morph between shots, characters pop in and out, and quality collapses as length grows. Their 2026 framework, InfinityStory, attacks all three, with character-aware transitions as its signature.

A background-consistent pipeline holds scenery, character identity, and spatial relations steady across scenes. A transition module then choreographs smooth shot changes for several subjects entering or leaving the frame at once, beyond the single-subject limits of earlier work. A synthetic dataset of ten thousand multi-subject transition sequences trains the skill. On the standard VBench suite, InfinityStory records the highest background and subject consistency scores and the best overall average rank.
arxiv-2604-00046: Pagels and team propose a large language model to spot and measure Enterprise Architecture Debt in documentation. It arises from poor decisions and mismatched parts harming an IT estate. Early signs, EA Smells, are found by hand or from set files. Using design science, the team builds and tests a tool for auto finding. The tool ingests process notes and plans, applies fine-tuned models, and outputs smells. A case study with fake firm documents, against a custom GPT-based model, shows language models detect known smells in text.
arxiv-2604-00146: Chaudhuri and Mukherjee give unitary representations of mixed braid groups on cohomology groups of Abelian branched covers over the complex projective line. Complex reflections generate the image of each representation. The authors also link the construction to the multivariate Burau representation, giving a full account of this monodromy picture. The paper works out the maps in full detail.
arxiv-2604-00346: Lee builds a forecasting method for gaps between orders in fast electronic markets, where waiting times cluster and stretch into long tails. His self-exciting residual point process keeps the observed shape of those gaps while preserving bursts and decay, and he checks that the process settles into a stable long-run pattern. Tests on very fast trading records beat several rival approaches at predicting the next gap.
arxiv-2604-00546: De Micheli and colleagues present a lightweight system for encrypted face recognition with GPU support. Face recognition runs client-server. The client turns a face into a compact embedding, and the server searches a store. Facial data is sensitive, so privacy concerns run deep. Fully homomorphic encryption allows encrypted search, but protocols cost heavily in compute and memory, burdened by rotation-key sets and bandwidth-bound operations. Building on HyDia, the team adds algorithmic improvements for edge clients, with BSGS-Diagonal, a fast, memory-efficient similarity algorithm.
arxiv-2604-00646: Salone and colleagues work out non-leptonic hyperon decays in relativistic chiral perturbation theory to next-to-leading order, the first such treatment. Recent lab gains prompted the work. Loop corrections are computed from ground octet and decuplet fields. Low-energy constants for weak transitions are gauged by resonance saturation, following a non-relativistic tree-level calculation. The spin-1/2-minus and spin-1/2-plus octets are used. The rest are fitted to decay amplitudes, giving a joint account of s- and p-wave amplitudes, though not tightly pinned. Resonances matter most.
arxiv-2604-00746: Deepanshu Kush proves an unconditional barrier to proving superpolynomial lower bounds for multilinear algebraic branching programs with the min-partition rank method. He exhibits a full-rank multilinear polynomial that a polynomial-size branching program can compute, so the method cannot deliver the separation. His proof settles an open problem about the size of 1-balanced-chain set systems, showing the key quantity grows only polynomially.
arxiv-2604-00946: Zain and colleagues study near-Earth asteroids in Main Belt-crossing orbits, selecting objects brighter than magnitude 18 and integrating their orbits for 10 million years. Objects split by initial semi-major axis into three groups, with median lifetimes falling as axis grows, from about 13 million years to about 0.9 million years. Collisional erosion barely changes the global size distribution over a million years, though the asteroids spend much of their lives inside the Main Belt under frequent small impacts.
arxiv-2604-01246: Musielak, Fry, and Kanan consider complex scalar fields under a novel Klein-Gordon equation from gauge and group theories, at Schwarzschild black hole singularities. They show the field stays well-behaved near these singularities and reaches zero at both of them. The field also forms a scalar hair outside the event horizon, while the interior field is tachyonic and settles into its lowest-energy state at the central singularity. This behavior differs sharply from the minimally coupled Klein-Gordon equation, with implications for black hole interiors.
arxiv-2604-01546: Reinhardt and colleagues propose Tensor-ComBat, a spatial matching for brain scan data that gauges and removes tech shifts between voxel images from sites or scanners. Tensor-ComBat uses a Bayes tensor model to gauge spread scanner effects via a low-rank PARAFAC split, then removes them via a ComBat step. Unlike plain ComBat, which treats voxels as same, Tensor-ComBat uses voxel layouts when gauging settings, aiding matching. Applied to over 2100 T1w-MRI scans in ADNI-1, it shows greater effect removal, body prediction, and better reruns versus ComBat.
arxiv-2604-01646: Jung and colleagues propose a method for thinly labeled monocular 3D finding with two key modules. Monocular 3D finding does well on densely labeled sets but falters when labels cover only some objects, a common setting given the high cost of 3D labels. Road-Aware Patch Augmentation uses sparse labels by placing cut patches onto road regions while keeping 3D shape fit. Prototype-Based Filtering makes good pseudo-labels by sifting guesses through model match and depth doubt, picking labels matching learned models with reliable depth guesses.
arxiv-2604-01746: Macheda and Sohier study interactions between electrons and phonons, and among electrons themselves, over long ranges in doped 2D materials, including interlayer couplings in van der Waals stacks. They assess transport effects with dynamic coupled Boltzmann equations for electrons and for active excitations. The theory claims validity and is applied to simple parabolic models and to a boron-nitride-encapsulated graphene system in a second paper. Dynamic screening proves fundamental to describing transport right, in particular polar phonon scattering, whether from the semiconductor or nearby layers.
arxiv-2604-01846: He tracks p-adic Hodge parameters for semistable Galois representations with regular weights. Merging crystalline case methods with counts of extension groups for Steinberg representations, he reads the full parameter data off Steinberg pieces and the crystalline data between them. The results also restate in geometric and Lie algebraic terms on flag varieties. He builds an explicit locally analytic representation and shows that when its monodromy rank is small, it pins down the target.
arxiv-2604-02246: Mahato and Blaschke study the thermodynamics of a graphene inspired Gross Neveu model in two plus one dimensions. Focusing on entropy from Gaussian fluctuations beyond mean field, they find fluctuations contribute nearly as much as the mean field itself. Feedback from fluctuations to the mean field must be included, cutting mainly Landau damping contributions. A generalized Beth Uhlenbeck treatment suppresses low energy terms while keeping bound state effects, giving a sharper crossover in the degrees of freedom.
arxiv-2604-02346: Liu and colleagues benchmark language models for drug discovery with DrugPlayGround. The frame tests text accounts of drug traits, drug protein interactions, and body responses to drug perturbations. It also pairs predictions with expert guided reasons to probe chemical and life science reasoning. The goal is an objective account of where language models help or falter against older drug discovery platforms across all stages of the pipeline.
arxiv-2604-02546: Mao and four colleagues propose UniScene3D, a transformer system that learns one shared 3D scene code from multi-view RGB-Pointmap inputs. It borrows priors from a pretrained 2D base model and enforces shape and meaning consistency across views through two alignment tricks. Fine-tuning on viewpoint grounding, retrieval, classification and 3D question answering reaches top results in low-shot and task-specific settings.
arxiv-2604-02646: Abe and three colleagues refine bounds on contractible edges that preserve 4-connectedness in graphs, focusing on plane triangulations. They show that a 4-connected plane triangulation with at least seven vertices holds at least as many such edges as the count of vertices of degree five or more, plus two. They also determine the extremal graphs that meet the bound.
arxiv-2604-02746: Chen, Shao and Shi study zero-free regions of the hard-core model partition function on finite graphs and their implications for free energy analyticity. Classical results reach the tree uniqueness threshold set by maximum degree, but the connective constant measures structural complexity more precisely for lattices. Defining the connective constant for finite graphs via self-avoiding walks, they prove zero-freeness below the threshold set by that constant.
arxiv-2604-02846: Shi and four colleagues propose adaptive local frequency filtering for Fourier-encoded implicit neural representations. Such models learn continuous signals from discrete samples. Fixed Fourier mappings use one frequency set everywhere, fitting signals with varying local spectra poorly and converging slowly on fine details. A parameter that varies in space tunes encoded Fourier components, sliding smoothly among low-pass, band-pass, and high-pass response across locations. The method improves reconstruction quality and speed over fixed-frequency baselines. Tests cover 2D image fitting, 3D shape work, and sparse data rebuilding.
arxiv-2604-02946: Nagano and five colleagues train models on synthetic data with help from provenance records made during synthesis. Each input region is marked as target or non-target, and gradients over non-target regions are suppressed. That push steers the model toward features of the target object itself, instead of quirks and artifacts left by synthesis. Tests across weakly supervised object localization, spatio-temporal action localization, and image classification show the method works across tasks and modalities.
arxiv-2604-03346: Wang and colleagues use quantum circuits to solve the partial differential equations behind portfolio choice. Their circuit builds a polynomial from tensor rank breakdown, cutting resource needs from exponential to polynomial when rank is modest. Built into quantum and quantum-inspired physics-informed networks, the models beat standard networks on the Merton problem while using far fewer weights.
arxiv-2604-03546: Ohno and Togawa revisit three ways to shrink large coefficients in quantum annealing Hamiltonians under minor-embedding rules. A wide coefficient range hurts results there. They test how far the methods shrink the range of the minor-embedded Hamiltonian. They also test sample scores on the D-Wave Advantage annealer. The interaction-extension method lifts sample scores well by shrinking the range. Bounded-coefficient integer encoding and the augmented Lagrangian method show only small effects.
arxiv-2604-04046: Jiale Huang and team named the dismagicker, a non-Clifford unitary gate that cuts non-stabilizerness, or magic, in quantum many-body states. Tools that cut entanglement are standard in tensor networks, but no matching tool existed for magic cutting. They steer states toward stabilizer states a classical machine can mimic, built by tuning within matrix product states. Joined with Clifford untying steps, the method raised scores for old-style simulation and quantum state setup.
arxiv-2604-04146: Lai and Nguyen extend a tiling count for cross-shaped regions built from overlapping Aztec rectangles. Ciucu had shown that the number of domino tilings of such a cruciform region follows a simple product formula. The authors generalize that result to a generating-function formula, which packages the counts across region sizes. The work grows out of Di Francesco's Aztec triangle conjecture and its connection to the twenty-vertex model.
arxiv-2604-04646: Cha and five colleagues propose the Flow Divergence Sampler, a training-free framework for flow matching. Flow models learn a target distribution from a marginal velocity field averaging sample velocities from a prior to target data. When sample velocities conflict at one state, the mean velocity can misguide samples toward low-density regions. This misguidance is quantified by the divergence of the velocity field. The sampler steers states toward clearer regions. As a plug-and-play framework for solvers, it improves fidelity across tasks including text-to-image synthesis.
arxiv-2604-04846: Mony and Dhir study the Bc meson spectrum with a Bayesian approach, testing three confining potentials: the Cornell form, a logarithmically modified version, and a screened Cornell form. They sample each potential's parameters by Markov chain Monte Carlo, keeping correlations among fitted values. The resulting distributions yield masses, spin splittings, mixing angles, and wave-function measures through the 6D multiplet, checked against Regge trajectories. Low-lying states stay stable across potentials, while higher states diverge as they probe larger distances, with growing uncertainty.
arxiv-2604-04946: Hu, Glatt, and Liu tackle phase drift in graph-based models for fluid dynamics, where forecasts stay plausible yet lose time alignment with observations. That drift limits digital twins and control, while retraining a frozen surrogate is costly and impractical. They ask whether drift can be corrected by steering latent space. Their phase-steering framework for pretrained CFD models pairs sparse autoencoders, which yield disentangled codes, with an intervention mechanism. Steering latent space aims to restore temporal alignment without new training.
arxiv-2604-05046: Kunnumkai and four co-authors ask whether gravitational-wave merger rates can explain the observed short gamma-ray burst rate. Binary neutron star detections are scarce in the latest LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA run, raising doubt that merger rates suffice. Using fourth-run merger constraints and published local burst rates, they test reconciliation. For burst rates near one to seven per cubic gigaparsec per year, if over 55 percent of binary neutron star mergers launch a jet, the current merger rate suffices.
arxiv-2604-05346: Gretarsson and ten colleagues study ruthenium tribromide, a layered magnet prized for Kitaev magnetism, where competing spin links frustrate ordinary order. With X-ray scattering tuned to ruthenium, they watch its zigzag spin pattern melt at the Neel point. Zigzag correlations survive well above that point, however, and shift strength along the stacking direction. Extended bromine orbitals strengthen links between layers, the team argues, locking in correlations across layers that the chloride cousin lacks.
arxiv-2604-05446: Lee and Kim improve mean estimation when labels are scarce but unlabeled traits abound. Their MEC method reweights labeled cases to match the target group, using split-sample fits and Bregman projections to stay steady when predictors err. It meets the efficiency bound under weaker rules, with coverage near its stated level and tighter gaps than prediction-powered rivals.
arxiv-2604-05546: Zhang and nine colleagues review fast inference for large vision-language models, where image tokens swamp cost across encoding, prefilling, and decoding. They sort tricks by life-cycle stage and by three axes: information density, long-context attention, and memory limits. The review ends with four frontiers, from hybrid compression to split-stage serving, backed by pilot tests.
arxiv-2604-05846: Sun and four colleagues turn graph learning into agentic navigation plus language-model inference with AgentGL. Graph-native tools enable multi-scale exploration, search-limited thinking balances accuracy and efficiency, and graph-shaped curriculum reinforcement learning steadies long-horizon policy learning. Gains reach up to about 18 percent on node classification and about 28 percent on link prediction.
arxiv-2604-05946: Spaeth and Roberts show that small ensemble size bends conditional reliability checks in weather forecasting. Finite samples shrink the slopes of spread-error links and reliability diagrams even for perfect forecasts, so flat slopes need not mean bad forecasts. They work out exact shrink formulas and give estimators from ensemble data alone, then show the bend bites hard in ECMWF sub-seasonal temperature forecasts.
arxiv-2604-06346: Alansary, Mohamed, and Hamdi propose severity-aware weighted loss for Arabic models. Fine-tuning treats all cases evenly, ignoring severity, though severe errors carry higher risk. Their method scales loss by soft severity probabilities, prioritizing critical interactions. Labels and scores come from an AraBERT-based classifier at loss level only. Experiments use the MAQA dataset of complaints and responses, across ten Arabic large language models. Standard fine-tuning yields modest improvements, while severity-aware optimization improves AraGPT2-Base from 59 to 66 percent and gains up to 12.1 percent over baselines.
arxiv-2604-06746: Chen, Liu, and Shao protect long-context inference from memory blowup with StructKV. As context windows pass one million tokens, key-value caches grow linearly and choke memory and bandwidth. Existing compressors rank tokens by local saliency at one layer, discarding tokens that act as global hubs yet look dormant there. StructKV aggregates attention across network depth to find those hubs, detects the best compression layer adaptively, and separates compute budget from storage budget. Tests on LongBench and RULER show it preserves long-range links and retrieval strength.
arxiv-2604-07046: Dabbaghi, García Lastra, and de Silva recast density models so they use the full bend of electron density rather than only its slope hints. Standard models lean on kinetic energy density or a density laplacian, which can blur apart one electron cases that look alike. The authors present a simple no fit model, theta PBE, and lay out a path to run it in full self agreement inside a common wave method. Tests show sound chemisorption energies, though bulk lattice spacings stay hard to pin.
arxiv-2604-07246: Elokda and three colleagues design a karma economy for sharing scarce charging power among electric vehicles. Each driver holds non-tradable karma tokens and bids them in each time slot, with winners paying their bids into a pool that is then redistributed. The scheme handles changing charge levels, private trip deadlines, and varying urgency. A stable equilibrium is shown to exist, and it balances deadline pressure against urgency better than standard scheduling rules.
arxiv-2604-07346: Borchia, Knolle, and Nunnenkamp show that links between particles can spread one-way motion from a bath to parts it never touches. Their test case is a line of spin-1/2 fermions with Hatsugai-Kohmoto links joining all pairs and a built bath. In that setup, the motion stays exactly solvable. Links reshape how excitations move and drive drift even in spin parts with no direct bath link. The same effect holds for short-range links in a driven Fermi-Hubbard chain, giving a solvable test bed for such motion.
arxiv-2604-07446: Bala and three colleagues build a Super-Grassmannian integral form for n-point functions in N equals 1 superconformal theory in three dimensions. Conformal, supersymmetry, and special superconformal invariance show up plainly through operator-valued delta-function constraints. Simple algebraic links among component correlators let any component follow from just one of them. The form also builds AdS4 boundary correlators with contact diagrams from pure exchange terms, shown by the Yang-Mills gluon four-point function.
arxiv-2604-08046: Zhao and nine colleagues tackle the integration bottleneck in RAG, where retrieved files often fail to change model answers, even when matching. Current research stresses lookup quality but overlooks a key failure: models ignore matching files that conflict with internal parametric memory. Resolving that conflict quietly in a single generation pass proves weak. Their GuarantRAG framework openly splits reasoning from evidence integration. An Inner-Answer from built-in knowledge alone captures the model's reasoning flow, while a Refer-Answer built with a contrastive training goal ensures faithful evidence use.
arxiv-2604-08146: Tian gives a simpler proof of a descent conjecture of Wittenberg for certain torsors. The conjecture says a smooth base inherits weak approximation with Brauer-Manin obstruction when every twist of a rationally connected torsor over it satisfies it. Tian proves the claim for certain torsors under connected linear groups, using Cao's descent formula. The argument offers an alternative route to Wittenberg's result in these cases.
arxiv-2604-08246: Carstensen and Tran present a local discontinuous Galerkin finite element method for convex minimization. Error control in convex minimization hinges on tight control of the discrete-exact minimal energy gap. Conforming discretizations for p-Laplace minimization give energy-difference bounds at optimal rates. Even for smooth solutions, known rates for higher-order non-conforming discretizations stay suboptimal. Thus popular a posteriori error control via the two-energy principle, generalizing hyper-circle identities, looks unbalanced. The authors offer a refined analysis as a new starting point.
arxiv-2604-08846: Luo and seven colleagues introduce DACO, dictionary aligned concept control for safeguarding multimodal language models. Prompt engineering, response classification, and fine tuning often fail against evolving malicious patterns, need query reruns, or cost heavily, while activation steering of a frozen model offers flexible control. DACO curates 15,000 multimodal concepts from over 400,000 caption image stimuli into concept directions, forming DACO-400K, and uses sparse coding plus a sparse autoencoder initialized from the dictionary to steer activations. Tests across models and safety benchmarks show much better safety with general capabilities intact.
arxiv-2604-08946: Fan, Huang, and Lei settle a long-open question for the compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations: do global smooth solutions exist for general large initial data? The answer is yes under ball-shaped symmetry on solid balls, with density-linked thickness meeting a BD-type entropy rule. By using the coupling between effective speed and speed, the authors prove bounds for key values, yielding density bounds. The result is the first for any large initial data in a truly multi-way domain with rich traits.
arxiv-2604-09146: Rivière, Malo, Varlin Grassi, and Prié study breaks in presence, moments when a distraction snaps a virtual reality user out of feeling present. From close interviews with 14 users of a height exposure program, they model 57 episodes in fine detail. Four patterns emerge: episodes users reflect on, episodes they discard, episodes tied to self-protection, and episodes with mixed signals. The authors read these against a model of presence and offer an awareness-based definition plus three design ideas.
arxiv-2604-09246: Ghosh, Sinha, and Stober improve voice masking for atypical speech in the DDSP-QbE pipeline. Its sawtooth drive signal has sharp jumps that cause aliasing, heard as buzz and distortion at higher pitches. The authors add voicing detection to gate the drive signal, swapping in filtered noise for unvoiced parts, and apply PolyBLEP correction to smooth each phase wrap. Together these changes give cleaner sound, fewer high-frequency flaws, and more natural speech, with no extra learnable parameters.
arxiv-2604-09346: Pierzyna, Basu, and Saathof present OTProf, a deep-learning method building fine-grained optical turbulence profiles from coarse ERA5 data. Accurate profiles matter for ground-based optical astronomy and free-space optical links. OTProf builds on Squeezeformer, tweaked for super-resolution with grid-free blending in latent space. Tested in Dutch sites against Weather Research and Forecast data, it beats the Hufnagel benchmark on structure, Fried value, and twinkle index, though Canary Islands results drop.
arxiv-2604-09546: Averkiou, Musso, and Yu build the first smooth multi-vortex solution of the three-dimensional Euler equations for fluids that cannot be squeezed. It shows a cluster of collapsing helical filaments. By adapting gluing methods to helical flows without swirl, they keep the cross-sectional vorticity in a bounded region for all time. The result extends earlier collapsing setups with fast-fading vortex cores and variational answers once confined to endless cylindrical domains.
arxiv-2604-09746: Sinha and nine co-authors build CONSCIENTIA, a multi-agent simulation in a simplified New York model testing agent strategy. Blue agents aim for fast destinations, while Red agents steer them toward billboard-heavy routes for ad revenue, forcing choices about trust and deception. Policies update across rounds through Kahneman-Tversky Optimization to cut billboard exposure while staying efficient. The best Blue policy lifts task success from 46 percent to about 57 percent, though susceptibility stays near 71 percent. Later policies cooperate more selectively, but resisting steering trades against task completion.
arxiv-2604-09946: Rezk and five co-authors argue public checks are key for ranked search, where expert reviews miss how blame, harm, and trust feel. Three workshops with 21 people pitted a lexical ranker against a neural ranker across four tasks, varying clarity and controls, including a hostile rigged ranking. People built causal stories linking system traits to broader impacts, yielding a map spanning knowledge, image, system, and downstream social impacts. Yet felt skill and built trust dulled care, letting rigging pass unseen, and people wanted sight into the full works plus recourse.
arxiv-2604-10146: Rao, Keviczky, and Rajan build CRMGP, a consensus-based recursive multi-output Gaussian process for vector fields. Multi-output Gaussian processes give sound learning with uncertainty, but are hard to deploy at scale in distributed settings. CRMGP pairs recursive inference on shared basis vectors with neighbour consensus updates. The result supports parallel distributed learning with bounded work per step, while keeping links between outputs and honest uncertainty. Tests on synthetic wind fields and real LiDAR data show competitive predictions and trustworthy uncertainty scores, a scalable option for multi-agent sensing.
arxiv-2604-10246: Li, Vosselman, and Nex compare traditional and learning-based multi-view stereo for photogrammetric reconstruction. Traditional COLMAP-style reconstruction gives high accuracy but runs slowly. Learning methods are geometry-guided or end-to-end, tested on two aerial scenes. COLMAP stays reliable and consistent but slow, while learning methods match features better and are more robust where traditional registration fails. Geometry-guided methods need preparation and COLMAP priors, while end-to-end DUSt3R and VGGT match COLMAP accuracy and coverage faster, though with larger residuals in hard scenes.
arxiv-2604-10746: Sattar and five colleagues investigate half-quantized anomalous Hall conductance in topological-insulator and ferromagnet stacks, a parity-anomaly case. A ferromagnetic layer against one surface of a thin topological-insulator slab breaks time-reversal symmetry and opens a gap in the Dirac-like surface spectrum. The result supports chiral currents with a single spin channel, yielding half-quantized conductance of e squared over 2h. With first-principles and tight-binding methods on three stacks, they map the gap and sidewall states and discuss what blocks exact half-quantization.
arxiv-2604-11046: Patra and two colleagues investigate how transition density affects neutron star equations of state. They match a nucleonic description at low densities to a high density extension based on a sound-speed form. Using four nucleonic models from nuclear matter values, they isolate low density and transition density effects on neutron star observables. Within their smooth matching rule, radii and tidal effects retain sensitivity to the low density equation of state. This holds at transition densities around twice saturation density, and matching gaps there spread into the high density extension.
arxiv-2604-11146: Colybes and two colleagues introduce a Full Compression Pipeline for green federated learning (FL) in constrained settings. FL enables joint training across spread clients without sharing raw data, preserving privacy. It often suffers heavy communication and compute overhead, limiting scale. It joins pruning, quantization, and Huffman encoding into one framework. By compressing local models and payloads, it greatly reduces transfer costs while keeping accuracy high. In one scenario, training runs more than 60 percent faster with only a 2 percent scores drop.
arxiv-2604-11546: Huang and four colleagues present RLSpoofer, a light black-box test of LLM watermark spoofing. Current tests demand large datasets and white-box access, leaving black-box spoofing poorly measured. From a distributional view, they prove a local capacity bottleneck on mass movable under KL-bounded updates without losing meaning. RLSpoofer, a reinforcement-learning attack, needs only 100 human-watermarked pairs and zero internals access. It lets a 4B model reach a 62.0 percent spoof success rate on PF-marked texts, dwarfing the 6 percent of baselines trained on up to 10,000 samples.
arxiv-2604-12046: Liu and Wang propose CURE, a framework for long-form factuality by teaching models claim-level uncertainty reasoning, rather than one whole score. A Claim-Aware Protocol splits outputs into atomic claims paired with estimates. Multi-stage training then aligns scores with claim truth and optimises for facts, enabling selective prediction, skipping uncertain claims at inference. On four factuality benchmarks, CURE beats supervised and reinforcement-learning baselines while keeping recall. It raises claim-level accuracy by up to 39.9 percent on Biography, with a 16.0 percent AUROC increase on FactBench.
arxiv-2604-12146: Estrada asks when infinite permutation groups that arise as automorphism groups of generic structures admit transitive extensions. The question was largely studied for finite groups, so he builds combinatorial tools for the infinite case. He proves edge-colored hypergraphs admit such extensions only when the color count is a power of two, and hypertournaments only when the parameter is even, among other results.
arxiv-2604-12446: Zida Li and five colleagues expose hidden backdoors in text-to-image diffusion models. Backdoors hide triggers in natural inputs, defeating defenses that hunt visible anomalies. Their approach perturbs cross-attention scaling and watches how responses evolve across denoising steps. Benign and backdoor inputs diverge systematically in that response pattern. The SET detector learns a compact benign response space from few clean samples. New inputs are flagged by deviation from that space, with no attack knowledge needed. It beats the best baseline by 9.1 percent on AUROC and 6.5 percent on accuracy.
arxiv-2604-12646: G. Singh and three colleagues control strong-field ionization with quantum light statistics. A bichromatic field pairs a strong coherent driver with weak bright squeezed vacuum. Simulations show electron momentum patterns far more asymmetric than classical fields allow. The boost traces to the squeezed vacuum's odd statistics. Field swings strongly shift tunneling odds. Electron motion after escape stays unchanged. Control aids mapping of ionization pathways. Sub-cycle dynamics become readable from field data.
arxiv-2604-12846: Andreas Čap and Zhangwen Guo build elementary tools for path geometries. Path geometries encode systems of second-order ordinary differential equations. They are parabolic geometries, hard to study with standard tools. General methods use Cartan geometry and stay hard to reach. The authors define distinguished connections like Webster-Tanaka connections in CR geometry. Choices are indexed by sections of a natural line bundle. The Schouten tensor and its dependence are described. A smaller subclass of Weyl structures has no analog elsewhere.
arxiv-2604-12946: Hayden Prairie and three colleagues stabilize looped language models with Parcae. Fixed-depth models scale quality through size or data. Looped models reuse one block, but training often explodes or spikes. Parcae treats looping as a nonlinear dynamical system over residuals. Large spectral norms in injection parameters cause the instability. Discretizing a negative diagonal parameterization caps those norms. Parcae cuts validation perplexity up to 6.3 percent over prior models. Looping and data should grow together under fixed compute.
arxiv-2604-13046: Reis and five colleagues replace passive, always-on sensor logging with selective collection driven by user intent. Their framework pairs plain-language requests with a formally specified domain-specific language, letting language models write checkable trigger programs across cameras, LiDAR, and system telemetry. Tests on vehicle and robot perception show steadier output and faster execution than free-form code, with detection intact.
arxiv-2604-13146: Bakircioglu introduces the flavoured lattice Schwinger model, a one-plus-one-dimensional U(1) gauge theory that solves fermion doubling by staggering a Z2 flavour degree of freedom instead of chirality. Unlike standard approaches it preserves an exact axial U(1) symmetry at finite lattice spacing, and its continuum limit is the two-flavour massless Schwinger model. The central result is a well-defined lattice axial charge whose non-conservation arises directly from minimal gauge coupling. A particle-hole transformation exposes a hidden chiral symmetry.
arxiv-2604-13246: Bucur, Gentile, and Henrot sharpen Kröger's upper bounds for vibration frequencies of convex shapes under Neumann boundary conditions. For the kth frequency they prove a bound that subtracts a positive term tied to the second-largest axis of the shape's John ellipsoid, scaled by its diameter. The gap grows when the shape departs from the extremal form, and in the plane for the first frequency they also pin down the constant explicitly.
arxiv-2604-13346: Wang and nine colleagues introduce AgentSPEX, a language for specifying language-model agent workflows with explicit control flow and modular structure. Reactive prompting leaves control flow and state implicit, while frameworks like LangGraph and DSPy tie workflow logic tightly to Python. AgentSPEX supports typed steps, branching, loops, parallel execution, reusable submodules, and explicit state, executed in a harness with tools, sandboxing, checkpointing, and logging. A visual editor aids authoring, and a user study finds it more interpretable than a popular rival framework.
arxiv-2604-13746: Liang and nine colleagues reconstruct long, fast-moving dynamic scenes with ClipGStream, a clip-stream Gaussian splatting framework. Frame-stream methods scale but flicker, while clip methods stay locally consistent at high memory cost and limited length. ClipGStream optimizes at the clip level, modeling motion with clip-independent spatio-temporal fields plus residual anchor compensation, while inherited anchors and decoders keep structure consistent across clips. The result is scalable, flicker-free reconstruction with high temporal coherence and lower memory use.
arxiv-2604-13946: Doan and colleagues let plan and code modules take turns during debugging, rather than following a fixed plan or working in isolation. Their CollabCoder framework picks whichever module should run next through collaborative decision-making. On harder benchmarks the approach beats strong baselines by 11 to 20 percent while saving 4 to 10 API calls per run, with gains growing as tasks get harder.
arxiv-2604-14046: Diez and Guajardo show merons, the non-Abelian building blocks of instantons, live beyond Yang-Mills theory. A broad class of gauge theories supports them under the right conditions. Including gravity's response, meron-sourced black holes and Euclidean wormholes extend in turn. Kinks in constant-curvature backgrounds get smoothed. The framework also yields a regular black hole from truly non-Abelian fields and keeps meron effects like spin from isospin.
arxiv-2604-14146: Ladovrechis predicts a new anisotropic non-Fermi liquid born from a three-dimensional Berry-dipole semimetal under long-range Coulomb forces. The semimetal sits at the edge between a Hopf insulator and a trivial insulator, where topology plus interactions yield a phase with a bigger Berry-dipole moment. With large-N analysis and an epsilon expansion in a renormalization-group scheme, he works out how key measures scale with energy and temperature. He sketches a test to probe the phase.
arxiv-2604-14446: Yoon and seven colleagues demonstrate a probabilistic bit unit cell that pairs superparamagnetic tunnel junctions with 130-nanometer CMOS technology. The junction's resistance fluctuations drive a matching fluctuating digital output voltage, tunable through the input voltage. Crossing the CMOS-integration threshold has blocked scaling of junction-based probabilistic systems, and this cell shows such integration working. The result establishes feasible CMOS-compatible probabilistic circuits and a step toward scalable hardware for hard optimization and learning problems.
arxiv-2604-14746: Li, Zhang, and Zhang replace blind random tweaks in graph contrastive learning with a meaning-aware split. Their SDM-SCR framework first has a language model parse raw node attributes into task-focused signal views and noise views. A spectral filter then enforces consistency only on the signal side, since signals vary smoothly across the graph while noise sits at high frequencies. That guard keeps language-model hallucinations out without blurring real structure. Tests showed top accuracy and efficiency for text-attributed graphs.
arxiv-2604-15246: Caputo and others model how obstacles block 2D bistable reaction-diffusion fronts. Using a conservation law, they show the total of the reaction term acts as the front driving force. Paired with the exact 1D traveling wave, this yields a reduced model that predicts blocking points. Clear rules cover a waveguide joined to a cone-shaped region for widths below 4, and the model matches test runs and reaches checkerboard blocks.
arxiv-2604-15646: Roy Chowdhury and seven colleagues demo FD-NL2SQL, a feedback-driven assistant that turns clinicians' natural-language questions into SQL over oncology trial databases. A schema-aware model splits questions into predicate sub-questions, pulls expert-checked samples by embedding closeness, and builds checked SQL. Clinician edits and logic-based SQL tweaks with non-empty results feed the example bank, so the system gets better with use without added annotation.
arxiv-2604-16046: Clifton and three colleagues introduce a colorful version of separating path systems, in which two edges can only be separated by two paths of distinct colors. They calculate the minimum sizes of such systems for various standard graph classes and numbers of colors. With respect to this setup, they identify three possible asymptotic behaviors for a graph class as colors go to infinity, and find a wide range of examples displaying each behavior.
arxiv-2604-16246: Duque, Dudarev, Kermode, and Hudson bridge atom-scale and continuum accounts of nanoscale dislocation loops in tungsten, which matter for predicting long-term irradiation damage. Continuum models blow up unrealistically near the defect core, yet capture atom-scale displacements far away. Their linear elastic model, checked against atomistic simulations, agrees well with far-field behaviour when loops sit far from material boundaries, and shows matching decay rates.
arxiv-2604-16346: Corga Da Silva and eight co-authors pilot DR. INFO, an agentic AI medical helper, at the point of care in Portuguese sites. Medical paperwork and information search consume over half of doctors' working hours, driving strain and burnout, while hallucination and source trust worries limit AI uptake. In a forward-looking single-arm pilot, 29 doctors and medical students used DR. INFO over five working days across two weeks. Daily Likert-scale ratings and a final Net Promoter Score assess time saving and choice support.
arxiv-2604-16946: Wang studies Takesaki duality for weak-star closed Lp-operator crossed products, extending a classic von Neumann algebra duality to a wider setting. He builds a homomorphism from the double crossed product to an operator tensor product and pins down exactly when it is an isomorphism. The map is an isomorphism exactly when p equals 2 or the group is finite, and an isometric isomorphism exactly when p equals 2 or the group is trivial.
arxiv-2604-17146: Bényi and Nkonkobe study combinations of the degenerate and incomplete Stirling numbers of the second kind, two variants of the classic numbers that count ways to partition sets into blocks. Using a combinatorial approach, they provide asymptotic results describing how these combined numbers behave at large scales. The results give long-run approximations rather than exact closed forms.
arxiv-2604-17246: Islam, Pugh, and Bondarev present a study of Raman scatter for a two-level atom near a thin film holding aligned single-wall tubes. More broadly, their model unifies near-field boosts for films, with such tube films as the example. Focus falls on inbound photon settings such as light angle and entry angle against the tube axis. From the cross-section, they show a boost up to 10,000-fold, for both p- and s-polarized light.
arxiv-2604-17446: Saikia and eight colleagues test whether hyperspectral imaging beats ordinary color cameras for finding and matching keypoints in minimally invasive surgery. Poor texture and tricky lighting defeat many RGB pipelines, so their HyKey model blends spatial and spectral cues through a hybrid 3D-2D network. Trained on a robot-collected dual-camera dataset of ex-vivo organs, it beat RGB baselines including SuperPoint and ALIKE. Mean matching accuracy reached about 97 percent, with pose accuracy about 67 percent at ten degrees, supporting steadier 3D reconstruction in surgery.
arxiv-2604-17746: Cheng and colleagues test cosmic isotropy using gravity waves and gamma-ray bursts. Hints of anisotropies in supernova, microwave background, and burst data remain open. The cosmological principle asserts a smooth Universe at scale, though other models can produce uneven skies through local lumps or exotic physics. Using the O4a LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA release and GRBWeb, listing bursts since 1991, the team checks whether sky spots and burst traits are isotropic after bias fix. Angular power spectra and two-point links are set against fake data.
arxiv-2604-18046: Zhong and four colleagues present EvoMarket, a multi-agent financial market simulator built for intervention experiments across assets and days. It couples a fast execution core with mechanisms such as price limits, market calendars, opening call auctions, and next-day settlement. An oracle-guided self-calibration mechanism treats microstructure gaps as missing order flow, synthesizing corrective orders at checkpoints. Tests on China A-share order flow and limit order book data show tight replay alignment over five trading days, with performance scaling as order rates and breadth grow.
arxiv-2604-18346: Barakat, Talleux, and Zickgraf implement the biset category of finite groups inside the CAP system for algorithmic category theory. Bisets compose through a Kleisli setup built from a biadjunction monad, resting on the coequalizer-completion fact of a one-object groupoid. That universal property gives a clean abstract reading of the Schreier-Sims orbit algorithm. The implementation leans on every aspect of that method, stacking standard building blocks into a tower.
arxiv-2604-18446: Szołdra, Palmero, and Schmelcher bring recurrence analysis, a standard time-series tool, to quantum many-body motion. Such plots sketch mock or lab data, while its measures extract number scores. Applied to sudden jumps from the paramagnetic ground state in the 1D transverse-field Ising model, plots shift from nearly regular patterns deep in the ordered phase. At the tipping point, multi-scale shapes take over. The measures recover the tipping field strength blind, opening label-free spotting of quantum phase shifts.
arxiv-2604-18546: Al Taha and Bitar propose a robust approach to risk-aware estimation from signals. Both signals are random vectors with a joint distribution assumed in a type-2 Wasserstein ball, the ambiguity set. Quality is judged by tail value-at-risk of squared error. Their main result: when the nominal center has finite support, affine estimators best limiting worst-case CVaR can be found via a tractable semidefinite program. On bulk power price outlook with real data, they deliver smaller out-of-sample CVaR of squared error than rivals.
arxiv-2604-18646: Tanboga offers stable transport meta-analysis, a nuisance-anchor gauge modeling anchor-linked spread without shifting it to the target. It joins a weighted-mean loss with a scale-tuned softmax loss, plus a sign-stability check with a two-term holdback rule. In a set ADEMP test over six cases, it cuts bias against raw pooling and lifts coverage where Wald bands fail. Top trial coverage runs 85 versus 1 percent; tangled anchor 86 versus 34 percent; anchor shift 91 versus 60 percent. Where signs flip, the holdback rule fires in about 84 percent of repeats.
arxiv-2604-18846: Ma and Li address trainability in variational quantum objectives beyond the standard barren plateau template. They show it admits a fixed observable representation exactly when the loss is affine in the measured statistics. This marks the boundary of the standard concentration based proof template. Beyond the affine regime, a chain rule decomposition reveals three governing factors: model responsivity, loss side signal, and transmittance. Bounded gradient losses inherit suppression, while amplification capable losses can counteract it.
arxiv-2604-18946: In and three colleagues argue that safety lapses in large reasoning models stem from the reasoning structure itself. They propose AltTrain, a post training method that reshapes that structure. AltTrain needs no reinforcement learning or reward design, only supervised fine tuning on 1,000 light examples. Tests across model backbones and sizes show strong safety alignment with robust generalization across reasoning, question answering, summarization, and multilingual tasks.
arxiv-2604-19746: Anumba and colleagues study how calibration errors in SALT3 training affect dark energy limits from next-generation supernova surveys. The Rubin Observatory and Roman telescope surveys should find over a million Type Ia supernovae, far more than current samples, with tighter control of systematic errors. One of the largest such errors is the accuracy of the light-curve model, which rests on survey photometric calibration. The team tests this by perturbing photometric zero-points and filter mean wavelengths in simulated survey data and tracing the errors through the analysis.
arxiv-2604-20346: Schneider and 63 colleagues report XRF 241001A, a soft X ray flash from SVOM with a broad line Type Ic supernova. X ray flashes are gamma ray bursts with prompt light below 30 keV, rarely caught before. At redshift near six tenths, the burst lasted 3.14 seconds, with low peak energy and an afterglow fit by an on axis relativistic jet. Early blue light plus JWST spectra pin a soft low luminosity collapsar from a weak on axis jet, the low energy soft tail of long gamma ray bursts.
arxiv-2604-20446: Litman explains why gradient descent on neural networks pushes the Hessian eigenvalue to the edge value 2 over the learning rate. He defines an edge coupling, a function over consecutive steps whose coefficient follows from the update rule. He derives a recurrence and a loss-change formula whose sums force curvature to the edge. Zeroing both coupling gradients sorts the fixed points from the period-two orbits. Near a fixed point, a half-amplitude function decides which directions support orbits and on which side of the rate they appear.
arxiv-2604-20646: Banerjee, Chardin, and Holanda extend properties of a pair of ideals, in Tor terms, to any number of ideals, including the rigidity property. Those extensions require a homological theory for spectral sequences arising from multiple complexes. From that theory come two new complexes for quotients by ideal sums and products, whose homologies connect through Tor-independence. For multigraded cases, they map where Tor modules live for quotients built from variable-generated ideal sums and products.
arxiv-2604-20746: Banno, Kawada, Takenawa, Denda, and Aizawa propose a virtual flood system that integrates 360-degree videos with 3D models built from 2D building footprints. Although 360-degree video environments offer a simple way to replicate real scenes, flood visualization in them typically requires geometry of the area. By extruding footprints to heights and aligning the models with 360-degree videos, the system enables flood visualization. They demonstrate the system in Memuro, Japan, an area vulnerable to flooding. A user study with residents showed that the system helps users envision local flood evacuation situations.
arxiv-2604-20946: Ahmetaj and colleagues sort out rival meanings for recursive shape languages, the schema tools that check RDF data. ShEx validators use greatest-fixpoint rules, while SHACL validators lean toward least fixpoints. That split puts shared use at risk. The team sets out one formal account that covers least fixpoints, greatest fixpoints, and supported models. It shows a duality between the two fixpoint styles on stratified parts, and finds large parts of the two languages equal in power.
arxiv-2604-21046: Ali Aghababaei-Harandi, Aude Sportisse, and Massih-Reza Amini reshape semi-supervised image learning by organizing the model's internal geometry instead of only thresholding its guesses. Their method pairs a FlexMatch-style loss with a regularization term that pushes representations toward a tidy Gaussian shape. On CIFAR-100, STL-10, and Tiny-ImageNet it beats prior baselines and converges far faster, cutting the cost of training on scarce labels.
arxiv-2604-21146: Yalcin Tur, Mihajlo Stojkovic, and Ulas Bagci speed up multi-modal MRI synthesis by starting from structure already present instead of pure noise. Their wavelet flow method maps the average of available scans to the missing contrast in just one or two steps, with one 82M-parameter model covering all four BraTS contrasts. It runs 250 to 1,000 times faster than diffusion rivals while landing within 1 to 2 dB of their image quality.
arxiv-2604-21446: Andrew Shin runs AI-Gram, a live social platform where every participant is an autonomous language-model agent posting and answering visual content, with no humans involved. Eight pre-registered experiments trace a three-act dynamic. First, agents spontaneously form image-to-image reply chains with social ties driven by personality, not looks. Next, styles prove stubborn: identities hold under exposure and even harden under attack. Finally, sovereign styles combine within chains into conversations at once subject-coherent and style-diverse, with themes cascading super-critically.
arxiv-2604-21646: Shunhong Deng and colleagues report DESI-HVS1, an old, low-mass, metal-poor star racing fast enough that it may be unbound from the Milky Way.
